name: fade + scroll + photo article

files.photo-article.js: createPhotoArticle(feed,{onOpen,onClose}); close()/destroy(). Native dialog, decode barrier, cancellable rectangle animation.
files.photo-article.css: Static responsive article layout and photo overlay styles.
files.reference.json: Source inspection, dependencies, layout tokens, adaptations and matching-viewport comparison.
files.GeistMono-ascii.woff2: Official Google Fonts Geist Mono variable printable-ASCII subset; source Figma font inaccessible via shell.

integration: Import CSS and createPhotoArticle. Mark button data-read-more inside data-scroll-item. Each item needs img, h1/h2, small and figcaption.
onOpen must suspend the caption controller; onClose reinitializes it with the existing400ms delay. Feed native scrolling controller remains read-only.
Destroy the dialog controller on page teardown. Native dialog/showModal and Web Animations are used; no external JS dependencies.
behavior: The complete article is laid out before animation and remains stationary. A fully decoded copy of the selected image covers it initially, then shrinks into the right-hand image frame. Object-fit:cover preserves aspect ratio while the crop changes.
The feed gradient and caption dissolve without an initial brightness jump. Article scrolling remains locked until opening finishes.
The top-right X or Escape reverses from the photo current rectangle, including an interrupted opening or scrolled article image. Article remains stationary while it is covered.

Background feed is inert and locked during reading; normal close restores the existing feed position without a scroll write and restores keyboard focus. Resize recovery aligns the original photo only when dimensions actually changed.
Pending image/font preparation is canceled if user moves the feed. Failed image copies do not expose a blank cover.
Reduced-motion preference removes traveling/fade animations. Resizing or changing that preference during movement cancels/retargets safely.
Below800px the article follows the reference image-first stack, rather than squeezing readable text beside a narrow photo.
content: Clearly labeled sample article, selected existing photo title and alt description; final blog content was not supplied.
